origins.section: Rounding Up, or to the Nearest Whole, Can Break the Budget
Rounding Down Keeps This Model's Rows, and Still Misses the Best Plan
Rounding Down Then Filling Gives an Allowed Plan, Never a Proof

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-nearest: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-nearest: Paying for all of P022 instead adds $1,220k, so the plan spends $39,610k against $38,390k.
recorded.prompt:q-down-geq: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-down-geq: Rounding down is safe only for rows like these, where lowering a variable can never break them. A **≥ row** (a minimum to reach) is the opposite. ... Rounding down drops the 0.67 of D and the plan clears half the requirement.
recorded.prompt:q-fill-proof: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-fill-proof: The LP gives half the missing information: its value, $25,451.27k, is a ceiling no plan can pass, so the filled plan is at most $161.27k short.

recorded.prompt:q-nearest:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-nearest:a: Rounding to the nearest broke the budget 13 times in 30: every share it rounds up adds spend the LP never had.
recorded.prompt:q-nearest:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-nearest:c: Applying the rule "**Rounding to the nearest** funds a project when its share is 0.5 or more": 0.6 is funded whole, not dropped.
recorded.prompt:q-nearest:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-nearest:d: "The LP had already spent the budget to the dollar ... its 0.522 of P022 the remaining $1,330k. Paying for all of P022 instead adds $1,220k": only the unpaid share is added, not the whole cost.
recorded.prompt:q-down-geq:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-down-geq:a: A **≥ row** (a minimum to reach) is the opposite. The pole row says "at least 120", so it is a minimum, not a maximum.
recorded.prompt:q-down-geq:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-down-geq:b: By application of "every capex is positive, so lowering any x_i from a fraction to 0 lowers spend": dropping half of V lowers cost. In trap 2 (least cost) the failure named is "clears 200 km of the 400 required", not a higher cost.
recorded.prompt:q-down-geq:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-down-geq:c: Trap 2 shows rounding down does produce a plan: "round down: ['C'], clears 200 km of the 400 required". The failure is the broken minimum, not a missing plan.
recorded.prompt:q-fill-proof:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-fill-proof:b: Without that solve, all the filled plan tells you is that $25,290k is achievable. What it cannot tell you is whether $25,336k, or $27,000k, is.
recorded.prompt:q-fill-proof:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-fill-proof:c: **Rounding down then filling gives an allowed plan, never a proof.** Only a bound, or a MILP solve, says how far from the best it is.
recorded.prompt:q-fill-proof:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-fill-proof:d: its value ... is a ceiling no plan can pass, so the filled plan is at most $161.27k short. That is "at most", not "at least".
